signals.title: NZD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: NZD 1W avg +1.343% (n=4) vs USD -1.331% (n=7) produces a 2.674% G10 spread as fading Fed-hike bets and a surprise Treasury buyback weigh on the dollar. The NZD/USD close at 0.5982 is supported by a strong ESI divergence (NZD +5.1 vs USD -15.1) and negative real rate differentials favor the carry-unwind bid. The Sydney open is the catalyst for testing resistance at the 0.6000 psychological handle. Trade bias: Bullish NZD/USD into the open. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open. Risk: Recovery in US Treasury yields reverses the dollar's downward momentum.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Geopolitical Risk + Sentiment Skew
signals.text: Geopolitical escalation in the Strait of Hormuz and weakening Ifo sentiment in Germany create downside risk for EUR/USD despite its Friday close at 1.1678. EUR COT lev_net -76,035 (10th percentile) reflects extreme short positioning, but the 143bp OIS carry advantage for USD and bearish German growth outlook limit upside potential. The next ECB meeting (mkt: 96.0% hike priced) determines if the hike bias can offset geopolitical safe-haven flows into the dollar. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD toward 1.1634 (SMA200). Catalyst: Ifo Business Climate Index release. Risk: De-escalation in Middle East tensions triggers a short-squeeze in crowded EUR shorts.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Risk + Retail Extremes
signals.text: AUD COT LF long +49,749 (75% long) and 90% retail short sentiment create a volatile setup for the 0.7175 Friday close. While the 73bp OIS carry advantage favors AUD, the -10.3 ESI indicates persistent data misses that may undermine the RBA's hold-bias. The next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 29 Sep is the definitive catalyst for this rate-sensitive pair. Trade bias: Neutral/Bearish AUD/USD on exhaustion. Catalyst: Sydney open. Risk: AUD/USD breaks and holds above 0.7200, forcing a retail short-cover rally.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Yield Curve Regime
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 158.86 with a strong options put skew (RR -1.96) signaling elevated hedging demand for JPY strength despite a 264bp OIS carry disadvantage. The US 10Y bear steepener regime (2s10s +54.8bp) normally supports USD/JPY, but a correlation break (z=+2.10σ) suggests the pair is decoupling from safe-haven norms. The next BoJ meeting (mkt: 50% hike priced) on 18 Sep is the catalyst for resolving the yield gap tension. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY toward SMA200 at 158.33. Catalyst: Tokyo open. Risk: US 10Y yield surges above 4.80% re-establishing the carry-trade bid.

signals.title: USD/CAD — ESI Alignment + Crowded Short
signals.text: CAD COT LF net short -89,836 (13th percentile) creates significant squeeze risk for the 1.3763 Friday close as Canadian data continues to outperform (ESI +27.3). TD Securities notes tariff deals are unlikely to accelerate hikes, maintaining the 136bp OIS carry advantage for the USD. The next BoC meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 9 Sep is the catalyst for resolving the divergence between strong data and cautious policy. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD. Catalyst: Tokyo open. Risk: WTI oil falls below $85/bbl, weakening CAD support.
